classes.name: Levothyroxine (T4)
classes.description: Levothyroxine sodium: generic tablets and the brands Synthroid, Levoxyl, Unithroid, Euthyrox; Tirosint capsules; oral solutions Tirosint-SOL, Thyquidity, Ermeza. Generic tablets are AB-rated to specific reference brands, so a brand-only rule matters. Not liothyronine or desiccated thyroid.
classes.plainDescription: The standard daily pill that replaces thyroid hormone when your thyroid is underactive.

classes.name: Liothyronine (T3) and desiccated thyroid
classes.description: Liothyronine (Cytomel, generic tablets) and desiccated thyroid (Armour Thyroid, NP Thyroid; unapproved drugs under FDA enforcement action, often non-formulary; Adthyza reportedly discontinued). Levothyroxine is never this class's pick.
classes.plainDescription: Other thyroid pills, used alongside or instead of levothyroxine in some patients.

preferredAgent.sig: Healthy adults: full replacement about 1.6 mcg/kg once daily. Older adults or heart disease: start 12.5 to 25 mcg daily and raise by 12.5 to 25 mcg every 6 to 8 weeks. Adjust to TSH. Take on an empty stomach 30 to 60 minutes before breakfast (label).
preferredAgent.sigShort: Start per weight/age, titrate to TSH
preferredAgent.plainSig: One pill every morning on an empty stomach, 30 to 60 minutes before breakfast. Your dose is adjusted by blood tests.

records.verificationNote: PDL pp. 57-58 (HIC3 thyroid hormones). Generic levothyroxine tablets 25-300 mcg are all listed, no PA. The PDL lists Levoxyl and Unithroid with no PA and does not state that the brand is preferred over generic, so boglActive is false. Synthroid, Euthyrox, Tirosint, Tirosint-SOL, Thyquidity and Ermeza are not on the PDL. [Sonnet check 2026-11-13: Confirmed pp. 57-58. Desiccated thyroid belongs in thyroid-t3-ndt, not here; levothyroxine pick unchanged.]

records.verificationNote: PDL pp. 56-57 (HIC3 P3A), read by x-position. Liothyronine 5, 25 and 50 mcg tablets are listed, no PA. The PDL lists desiccated thyroid products as preferred with no PA. This conflicts with the class description ('often non-formulary'); the PDL is quoted, not the description. Cytomel brand and Adthyza are not on the PDL. [Sonnet check 2026-11-13: Confirmed p. 56-57: Armour, NP Thyroid, Niva, Renthyroid, Amerithroid, Evexithroid and generic Thyroid tablets all preferred, no PA, age 0+; liothyronine 5, 25, 50 mcg no PA (p. 57). Kept liothyronine as the pick and desiccated thyroid as alternatives (right class; they are FDA-unapproved and not interchangeable with levothyroxine, so they do not change the levothyroxine pick). Strength changed 5 mcg to 25 mcg so it delivers the label starting dose.]

records.verificationNote: Levothyroxine rows on PDF p.46 (generic, Tier 3, reference Synthroid) and p.47 (Synthroid, Tier 5). Generic is preferred over the brand, so no BOGL. Tirosint, Tirosint-SOL, Thyquidity, Ermeza, Levoxyl, Unithroid and Euthyrox have no row (searched all pages); recorded nonformulary under the closed-formulary statement. Judgment: the guide's 'All generic medications are covered' line (PDF p.3) conflicts with the closed-formulary wording, which governs unlisted drugs. [Sonnet check 2026-11-13: Brand-only nonformulary rules rest on the guide's own wording: "Brand name medications not listed in the medication list are not covered" (PDF p.2) and "Brand Name medications are covered only if they are included in the Closed Formulary list" (PDF p.3); exception route: Coverage Exception Process, PDF p.12 (printed XI). The p.5 line "any medications not on the formulary ... are not covered" is overridden for generics by "All generic medications are covered unless specifically excluded by your plan" (PDF p.3), so no generic is recorded as nonformulary from absence.]

records.verificationNote: Liothyronine rows on PDF p.46 (5, 25, 50 mcg, Tier 3, reference Cytomel). Pick uses 25 mcg rather than the brief's 5 mcg: the brief's rule says use the label starting dose and a strength that delivers it, and the label starting dose is 25 mcg daily. Desiccated thyroid products are listed at Tier 5 with no PA printed, so they are alternatives, not barriers. The FDA enforcement context for these products is not in the guide and is not recorded. Levothyroxine is not a pick here. [Sonnet check 2026-11-13: Brand-only nonformulary rules rest on the guide's own wording: "Brand name medications not listed in the medication list are not covered" (PDF p.2) and "Brand Name medications are covered only if they are included in the Closed Formulary list" (PDF p.3); exception route: Coverage Exception Process, PDF p.12 (printed XI). The p.5 line "any medications not on the formulary ... are not covered" is overridden for generics by "All generic medications are covered unless specifically excluded by your plan" (PDF p.3), so no generic is recorded as nonformulary from absence.] [Sonnet check 2026-11-13: Liothyronine 25 mcg: label starting dose is 25 mcg daily for adults (5 mcg daily in elderly or cardiac patients); the sig says 25 mcg to start, so strength and sig agree. Elderly patients start with the 5 mcg tablet (PDF p.46 lists 5, 25, 50 mcg).]
